prompt:
Compose a short message explaining that a shared document is ready for factual corrections, but that major changes to its structure will be considered separately. Please answer in roughly 160 words.

Write the requested response as one self-contained paragraph of plain text. Do not use a title, headings, bullet points, numbered lists, Markdown formatting, code fences, or line breaks. Include only the requested content, without any introductory or closing commentary from the assistant. Keep the approximate word target given in the task. If the task calls for an email, dialogue, steps, or calculations, express that content within the same paragraph.
base_prompt: Compose a short message explaining that a shared document is ready for factual corrections, but that major changes to its structure will be considered separately. Please answer in roughly 160 words.
text: The shared document is now ready for review and factual corrections. Please check the content carefully and identify any inaccurate, outdated, unclear, or unsupported information, then add comments or suggested edits where appropriate. At this stage, the main priority is to improve factual accuracy while preserving the document’s existing organization, flow, and overall purpose. If you believe a section needs clarification, you are welcome to explain the issue and suggest wording that resolves it without substantially changing the structure. Major revisions to the document’s organization, scope, sequence, or presentation will be considered separately after this factual review is complete. Keeping these two types of feedback distinct will help us address straightforward corrections efficiently and evaluate broader structural proposals thoughtfully. Once the factual review has been completed, we can discuss which larger changes would be most useful, how they would affect the document as a whole, and whether they should be incorporated in a later revision. Thank you for helping ensure that the shared document is accurate and reliable.
